key_insight: A discrete differential geometry phase-field model can couple large deformation, bending, and crack growth on the same thin-surface mesh, enabling realistic fracture simulation of highly flexible structures.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps predict and design damage-tolerant thin devices such as flexible electronics, where geometry change and fracture strongly influence performance.
method: Formulate membrane and bending elasticity from discrete geometric measures on a triangulated midsurface.
Define the phase field on the same surface and solve the coupled fracture problem with a staggered scheme plus active-set irreversibility.
Use degradation-deletion of nearly failed elements to allow full crack opening and post-fracture reconfiguration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with geometrically nonlinear finite-element results for 2D fracture and successful reproduction of 3D tearing behaviors, including crack convergence/coalescence and island-bridge snap-through.
watch_item: The degradation-deletion/topology reconstruction step may be sensitive to mesh quality and threshold choices, especially for complex crack paths.
paper_title: Phase-Field Fracture Simulation of Highly Deformable Thin Structures via a Discrete Differential Geometry Framework
